The usual reason is that "same" isn't really the same. Each time the parent re-renders, any prop that's an object, array, or function gets rebuilt fresh — like `onClick={() => ...}` or `style={{...}}` written inline. React compares by reference, so a brand-new object looks different even if it holds the same values, and the child re-renders.

A few common fixes:
1. Wrap the child in `React.memo` so it skips re-rendering when props are equal.
2. Wrap functions you pass down in `useCallback`, and objects/arrays in `useMemo`, so their reference stays stable between renders.
3. Check if the parent is re-rendering more than it needs to — sometimes the real fix is higher up, not on the child.

If you share the component code, I can point at the exact prop causing it.
